rows: A #2597 tab keeps about 90 MB more after every slider edit on Full Body, and none of the caches tried is the reason. A build "with the undo history capped at 2" still grew 92 MB per edit.
The undo history keeps it: whole page models, never cut. The "capped at 2" build had never applied its cap.
Andrew's compaction ported to #2597 (d41c7a0298), with the newest entry of each stack kept whole (f8ae6f2b9c). The same newest-entry change on #2635 (032fe3aca6): the latest undo and redo in 0.3 s.
Dev left alone, to get the compaction when #2469 merges (Matthew's call).
Time: every step is linear in the program; an undo costs about three edits. Two whole-program passes removed on #2635 (394552d5d0, bfa36a6ede), 31 to 46% off at the large sizes.
The outline's rebuild separated from the rest at each size: an undo is a redo plus a rebuild of the outline, a third of the undo. A redo rebuilds it only when its memo misses.
What one undo entry keeps as the program grows; why a restore rebuilds more syntax than an edit; dev's history; the balanced tree.
